scope.description: Third test function in the same harness file: a real three-voter group is elected for node 1, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is delivered to the quorum-relevant follower, a real campaign by node 3 is completed with the grants actually produced (pre-vote, vote), and then the new leader's first append is delivered to the deposed incumbent through the public Step path, observing the incumbent's soft state, the append's anchor, and the acknowledgement.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step.
Ticks are the target's logical clock; only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire.

All three nodes start from the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}); in this harness the followers never receive leader 1's term-2 entry, so the incumbent's committed prefix is (index=10, term=1) and its term-2 entry stays uncommitted.
The incumbent is not fed anything until the new leader's append, so its demotion is measured against that single append; the new leader's own commit value is emitted but not compared.
excluded: Any claim about the new leader's commit index: its operands (per-peer Match) are not fully observed through the public API here.

basis.prefix: Run the second test function's scenario to completion (real election for node 1, real heartbeat to the quorum-relevant follower, real MsgPreVote control, peer-form MsgForgetLeader, re-delivered pre-vote whose grant is fed back, resulting MsgVote whose grant is fed back), then take the new leader's first MsgApp, deliver it to the deposed incumbent, and emit the incumbent's post-append soft state plus the append's anchor (prev index/term), the appended entry, the acknowledgement and the incumbent's committed index before the append. Every value printed is read from the public Ready/Advance stream or BasicStatus after the corresponding Step returned.
basis.responsibility: The raft module owns the higher-term authority rule that a node sheds leadership when it learns a newer term, and owns whether the log it accepts continues the committed prefix it already had.

comparisons.description: Control: the quorum-relevant follower does not grant the pre-vote while its leader context is intact.
Defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader must not be accepted through the inbound path.
Disruption: an up-to-date candidate must not take leadership at a higher term while the incumbent is still serving.
Bound: the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append and sheds leadership on the higher term rather than fighting it.
Bound: the new leader's anchor is exactly the incumbent's committed prefix (index 10, term 1), so no committed index is lost by the change.
Bound: after the append the deposed incumbent follows the new leader rather than remaining leaderless.
